anomalies.observed: The Q1 symbol on sheet 1/1 carries the part/value name '2N7002', an N-channel enhancement MOSFET, wired as the high-side battery switch between J5 pin 1 and the /BAT bus net, with R5 (47k) pulling its gate to the source and SW1 pulling the gate to GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires Q1 to be an IRLML6402 P-channel MOSFET acting as a high-side battery disconnect switch: 'Q1 | IRLML6402 (P-ch MOSFET) | High-side battery disconnect switch: gates the battery connector (J5) onto the /BAT bus net' and 'closing it pulls Q1's gate (through R5, 47k) low enough to turn the P-FET on and connect the battery'.

evidence.quote: Q1 symbol labelled '2N7002' (sheet m5-pantilt.kicad_sch, 1/1, cell C) between J5 and the BAT net
Q1 | IRLML6402 (P-ch MOSFET) | High-side battery disconnect switch: gates the battery connector (J5) onto the /BAT bus net.

anomalies.impact: An N-channel device cannot be turned on by pulling its gate toward ground relative to a source sitting at battery potential; the gate drive network (R5 gate-to-source, SW1 gate-to-GND) is designed for a P-FET. With a 2N7002 in this position the high-side battery switch stays off (or behaves inverted), so the battery at J5 would never be connected to the /BAT bus and the board would not power from the battery.

parsed.summary: The drawing otherwise matches the spec (resistor/capacitor values, diodes, MAX3485 direction circuit, jumper annotations, and connector pinouts all check out), but Q1 is drawn as a 2N7002 N-channel MOSFET instead of the specified IRLML6402 P-channel high-side battery switch, which would break the battery power path.
